title: Rewrite observability bootstrap and introduce granular metric TTLs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: our current observability agent performs synchronous, heavyweight initialization of exporters, metric registries, and tracing hooks during service bootstrap. This causes increased cold-start latency, elevated memory usage at startup, and spikes in CPU for workloads that create many ephemeral metric labels. Goal: rewrite the bootstrap path to initialize a minimal fastpath on process start and lazily initialize heavy components (exporters, full label normalization pipeline) off the main thread. In addition introduce configurable, granular TTLs for metric families to evict stale label series and cap memory growth. Scope: - Replace synchronous exporter initialization with background worker and readiness gating. - Add metric-family-level TTL with default sensible values and a global low-memory policy. - Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK to latest stable 1.x and migrate our tracing hook adapter to the new SpanProcessor lifecycle. - Remove legacy StatsD adapter initialization from hot path; provide a deferred adapter shim. - Provide a compat mode for Dedicated/Private deployments that require deterministic exporter ordering. Out of scope: UI changes to Console; long-term cardinality reduction heuristics (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Service cold-start time reduced by >=30% measured on standard runtime image (benchmark script: scripts/bench/startup.sh)
Peak resident memory during startup reduced by >=25% for a normal model-serving workload
Metric series growth under synthetic churn workload (labels per request) is capped and obeys TTL policy documented in config
No observable change in end-to-end trace payloads for existing customers when compat mode enabled
OpenTelemetry SDK upgraded and all internal builds pass existing tracing integration tests
notes_and_decisions: 2026-03-02: Triage call - we agreed lazy init + readiness gating is highest-impact, will instrument with feature flag OBS_BOOTSTRAP_LAZY=true
Decision: prefer background thread for exporter creation rather than process-fork due to TLS and KMS interactions (security team input)
Trade-off: lazy init increases time-to-first-export metric/trace. Mitigation: emit first-export warmup hook and fallback to local ring buffer exporting until exporter is ready
We will land config defaults conservative: metric TTL default 24h for high-cardinality families, 1h for ephemeral internal metrics; allow override via METRIC_TTL_MAP env var
comments: 2026-03-03 — Liam O'Connor: Initial prototype landed in feature branch. Boot + background exporter worker implemented. Observed 28% reduction in median startup in local benchmarks.
2026-03-05 — SRE review (Maya Chen): Raised concern about readiness gating interaction with autoscaler. Added follow-up item to add readiness probe toggle.
2026-03-07 — PR feedback: Marcel (runtime): please add unit test for metric TTL eviction when cardinality threshold reached (see PR #5432 comments)

2026-03-09 — QA: ran churn workload where each request adds 3 label permutations. Without TTL memory grows unbounded; with TTL + eviction memory stabilized within limits. Attached heap profiles to PR.
Next steps: add compatibility-mode tests for Dedicated, update deployment docs, add migration notes for customers on custom exporters
risks: Lazy exporter init can delay first telemetry export causing delayed alerting for new services
Misconfigured TTL values may evict needed series too aggressively; we will provide audit logs for eviction events
OTel SDK upgrade could surface breaking changes for custom instrumentation; compat tests required
test_plan: Unit tests for TTL eviction policy and metric-family config parsing
Integration test that simulates startup with KMS-bound exporter initialization (Dedicated/Private) under compat mode
E2E smoke test to validate traces are emitted and collected when exporter initializes after service start
Load test with synthetic label churn to validate memory cap and eviction behavior
estimated_impact: Reduces customer-facing cold-start latency and long-term memory bloat for services with high label churn; improves observability pipeline stability during startup
release_notes_blurb: Optimize observability startup: introduce lazy initialization for exporters, configurable metric TTLs to prevent unbounded series growth, and upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK. Admins can opt into compatibility mode for deterministic exporter order.
